name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea at $535 a tonne after gas cuts to plants; Gulf tanker attacks continue near Hormuz
state: Egyptian granular urea rose to $535 a tonne FOB in November, about 17% above September's $457, after gas deliveries to nitrogen plants were cut by up to 20% from 1 Nov (UkrAgroConsult, 10 Nov). US retail fertiliser prices were mixed in the first week of November (Fertilizer Daily). Attacks on ships near Hormuz continued to 22 Nov, but no route closure or export restrictions by several exporters at once were found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher prices than in September, which can raise crop production costs and later food prices. Gulf shipping attacks remain a supply risk for urea and ammonia.
rubric_hit: Urea +17% in ~3 months < 60% Alert line; Gulf supply risk keeps Watch

sources.title: UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions
Fertilizer Daily — Retail fertilizer prices mixed, first week of November 2026

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
